Duplicate handling is verified: saving the same address again — even with a different scheme, no `www.`, or no trailing slash — now returns you to the **existing** entry instead of adding a copy. A genuinely different page still saves normally. I stopped the old screen so the updated one will load fresh.

**Open it again: [http://maker:4001](http://maker:4001)**

**Please try this sequence:**

1. Save any link (or use one already in your list).
2. Now paste **that same address again** and press **Save**.

Watch what happens: instead of a second copy appearing, a gentle note shows at the top (*"You already saved this — here it is"*) and the page glides to the existing entry and flashes it, so you land right on the one you already have.

One assumption I built in, which I'd like your judgment on: **I treat addresses as "the same link" even when they differ only by `http` vs `https`, a leading `www.`, or a trailing slash** — so `wikipedia.org` and `https://www.wikipedia.org/` count as one. That prevents near-identical duplicates. Does that match what *you'd* consider "the same link," or do you think of some of those as genuinely different pages?

And the core question: when you re-save something you already have, does being carried to the existing entry feel like the right response?
